name: Kotlin
description: Kotlin is the primary backend language. It is used across all Spring Boot modules of the project (app, carpool-domain, scheduler, mockingjay). Its expressiveness, null-safety and interoperability with the JVM ecosystem make it a consolidated choice. data class, extension functions and fun interface are extensively used to model the domain idiomatically.

name: Spring Boot 3
description: Spring Boot 3 is the backend application framework. It is used through the internal Gradle plugin eu.energypool.gradle-plugins.springboot, which bundles shared configuration (security, actuator, datasource, JMS). Spring Boot 3 targets Java 21 and brings notable improvements in AOT compilation and startup performance. All three backend services (app, scheduler, mockingjay) depend on it.

name: Angular 21
description: Angular 21 is the frontend framework of the project. The migration from Angular 17 was carried out to benefit from Standalone Components, the new build system based on @angular/build (esbuild), and performance improvements. Version 21 requires Node ≥ 24 and TypeScript 5.9. All components use the standalone approach without NgModules, simplifying the structure and improving tree-shaking.

name: TypeScript
description: TypeScript is the frontend language of the project. It is configured with strict: true and a shared tsconfig between the application and tests. Using TypeScript 5.9 with Angular 21 enables the latest language features (standard decorators, satisfies operator). The entire frontend codebase is statically typed, significantly reducing runtime errors.

name: RxJS
description: RxJS 7.8 is the reactive programming library used in Angular to manage asynchronous streams (HTTP calls, events). Its native integration with Angular (AsyncPipe, HttpClient) makes it an essential part of the frontend architecture. Version 7.x brings performance improvements and better compatibility with modern tree-shakers.

name: Vitest
description: Vitest is progressively replacing Karma/Jasmine as the frontend testing framework. Integrated via @ngx-energypool/vitest-tester, it relies on Vite for ultra-fast execution and natively supports ES modules. The project also uses @vitest/browser-playwright to run tests in a real Chromium browser, improving test fidelity compared to jsdom. This combination represents the future of frontend testing in the organisation.

name: Bootstrap 5
description: Bootstrap 5.3 is used as the frontend CSS foundation, integrated via the internal design system @ngx-energypool/ui-design. Direct usage in application code should be limited in favour of Energy Pool design system components, which encapsulate and customise Bootstrap. Prefer design system tokens and components over raw Bootstrap classes to ensure visual consistency across applications.

name: Highcharts
description: Highcharts 11.4 is the data visualisation library used in the frontend via the Angular wrapper @ngx-energypool/ui-design-highcharts. It provides a wide catalogue of chart types suited to business needs (power curves, histograms, gauges). Its integration through the internal package ensures consistent configuration and centralised licence management at organisation level.

name: ngx-translate
description: ngx-translate 17 is the internationalisation (i18n) solution for the frontend. Combined with ngx-translate-multi-http-loader to load multiple translation files, it enables modular label management. An internal tool (translationKeysConverter) generates a typed key file from the translation JSON, preventing typos in template keys.

name: Quartz Scheduler
description: Quartz Scheduler is used in the backend-scheduler module to execute scheduled jobs. It is wrapped by eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-quartz-api, which provides helpers for job creation and management. The scheduler is deployed as a standalone Spring Boot service, isolated from the main application, ensuring that batch processing does not impact API performance.

name: KSP (Kotlin Symbol Processing)
description: KSP (Kotlin Symbol Processing) is used in the carpool-domain module for compile-time code generation. The common-togglz-processor processor leverages KSP to automatically generate feature toggle constants from the @FeatureToggles enum. KSP is significantly faster than KAPT (Kotlin Annotation Processing Tool) because it operates directly on Kotlin ASTs without generating Java stubs. Its adoption is encouraged for any code generation needs within Kotlin modules.

name: Gradle (Kotlin DSL)
description: Gradle with the Kotlin DSL is the project build tool. It orchestrates a multi-module build covering six backend modules and the Angular frontend. The organisation has developed internal Gradle plugins (eu.energypool.gradle-plugins.*) that standardise configuration (Spring Boot, base JVM, security, database, Keycloak) and reduce duplication in build.gradle.kts files. The build cache is enabled via the buildcache plugin, significantly speeding up CI builds.

name: pnpm
description: pnpm is the mandatory package manager for the frontend. Its use is enforced via a preinstall script in package.json that blocks npm and yarn. pnpm offers superior performance and strict transitive dependency management (no phantom dependencies). npm and yarn must not be used on this project. The pnpm workspaces configuration is defined in pnpm-workspace.yaml.

name: SonarQube
description: SonarQube is the static code analysis tool for the backend. It is integrated into the CI workflow via the Gradle plugin eu.energypool.gradle-plugins.sonar and runs on every push to main and on every pull request. SonarQube analyses Kotlin code quality, duplications, potential bugs and security vulnerabilities. JaCoCo coverage results are forwarded to it for comprehensive analysis.

name: JaCoCo
description: JaCoCo is the code coverage measurement tool for the backend. It is configured with the jacoco-report-aggregation plugin in the app module to aggregate coverage across all project modules. The coverage report is generated on every ./gradlew check run and forwarded to SonarQube. Coverage is a quality criterion in the Definition of Done.

name: Liquibase
description: Liquibase is the database schema migration tool. It is used in the app and scheduler modules via the liquibase-core dependency. Migrations are executed automatically at application startup via common-database-init. This approach guarantees that the database schema is always consistent with the application code, across all environments.

name: Renovate
description: Renovate is the automated dependency update tool. It is configured via renovate.json and runs on a schedule defined in the renovate.yml workflow. Renovate creates automatic pull requests for npm, Gradle and Docker dependency updates, keeping the project up to date without manual effort. Auto-merge is configured for minor and patch updates after CI validation.

name: Release Please
description: Release Please is the release management and changelog tool. Combined with Conventional Commits, it analyses the git history to automatically generate a release PR with the appropriate semver bump and an updated CHANGELOG.md. Configuration is defined in release-please-config.json and .release-please-manifest.json. The publish-after-release-please.yml workflow triggers artefact publication after the release PR is merged.

name: TestContainers
description: TestContainers is used in backend integration tests to programmatically start Docker containers (PostgreSQL, Artemis). Integrated via eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-testcontainers, it guarantees test isolation and reproducibility. Tests run against real database and JMS broker instances, increasing confidence in integration tests compared to in-memory mocks.

name: Playwright
description: Playwright is integrated into the frontend test suite via @vitest/browser-playwright. It enables Vitest tests to run in a real Chromium browser (automatically installed during pnpm install via the postinstall script). This browser-based component testing approach is being progressively adopted and replaces jsdom-based tests, which do not faithfully reflect real browser behaviour.

name: ESLint + Prettier
description: ESLint (v9 with flat config) is used for static analysis of TypeScript code and Angular templates, via @angular-eslint and @typescript-eslint. Prettier (v3.2) handles code formatting with @trivago/prettier-plugin-sort-imports for automatic import sorting. Both tools are integrated together via eslint-config-prettier and eslint-plugin-prettier. Execution is integrated into CI via the lint workflow.

name: Super-linter
description: Super-linter is used in the lint.yml workflow to validate code quality on pull requests. It runs multiple linters against the various file types in the repository (YAML, Terraform, Markdown, etc.). Its usage is complementary to SonarQube, which covers Kotlin and TypeScript code. Configuration is managed via the .github/linters/actionlint.yml file.

name: AWS EKS
description: AWS EKS (Elastic Kubernetes Service) is the production execution platform for all applications. All services (backend, frontend, scheduler) are deployed on EKS as HelmRelease resources managed by FluxCD. The configuration includes horizontal pod autoscaling (HPA), liveness/readiness/startup probes, and pod disruption budgets. IRSA (IAM Roles for Service Accounts) is used to authenticate pods against AWS services without static credentials.

name: PostgreSQL 17
description: PostgreSQL 17 is the relational database management system of the project. It runs locally via Docker Compose (postgres:17.4-alpine) and in deployed environments via an internal Helm chart (chart/postgres). The connection uses the AWS JDBC Wrapper (aws-wrapper:postgresql) with the awsSecretsManager plugin to retrieve credentials from AWS Secrets Manager. Hibernate Envers handles change auditing.

name: Keycloak
description: Keycloak is the organisation's OIDC/OAuth2 Identity Provider (IdP). It handles user authentication and authorisation in the application. In local development, a custom Docker image (keycloak-custom_local) is provided with a pre-configured realm. In deployed environments, the UAT/prod Keycloak instance is referenced. The Gradle plugin eu.energypool.gradle-plugins.keycloak automates OIDC client configuration at deployment time.

name: Apache ActiveMQ Artemis
description: Apache ActiveMQ Artemis 2.33 is the JMS message broker used for asynchronous communication between services. It is integrated via eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-jms-api in the app and scheduler modules. Locally it runs via Docker Compose. JMS messages are secured by a JWT key mechanism defined in AWS secrets. Artemis supports AMQP, STOMP and OpenWire protocols in addition to native JMS.

name: FluxCD
description: FluxCD v2 is the GitOps operator that drives Kubernetes deployments. Deployment manifests (HelmRelease) are defined in the cd/ directory of the repository and continuously reconciled by FluxCD from the environment infrastructure repositories. This GitOps approach guarantees that the cluster state always matches the code in Git, with full deployment traceability.

name: Amazon ECR
description: Amazon ECR (Elastic Container Registry) is the organisation's Docker image registry. Application images (backend, frontend, scheduler) are published to ECR during the CI/CD workflow (cd-integration.yml, publish-after-release-please.yml). Images are referenced in HelmRelease resources using a semver-based tag. ECR is accessed from EKS via IRSA without static credentials.

name: OpenTelemetry Java Agent
description: OpenTelemetry Java Agent is enabled on backend services deployed on Kubernetes (otel.java.enabled: true in HelmRelease values). It automatically instruments Spring Boot for the collection of distributed traces, metrics and logs. This observability is essential in a multi-service architecture. The agent is injected by the internal Helm chart without any change to application code. Adoption is being progressively rolled out across all environments.

name: Terraform
description: Terraform is the Infrastructure as Code tool used to provision AWS resources (IAM, Secrets Manager, certificates, SSM parameters). The structure is organised into stacks (dev, prep, prod) with reusable modules. The Terraform version is pinned in the .terraform-version file. Terraform modules are automatically documented via the terraform-docs.yaml workflow. Terraform validation runs in the lint workflow on every PR.

name: Docker Compose
description: Docker Compose is used for the local development environment. It starts PostgreSQL, Apache ActiveMQ Artemis and Keycloak with pre-configured settings. The docker-compose.yaml file is the entry point for any developer joining the project. It is complemented by the Gradle plugin eu.energypool.gradle-plugins.database-dump, which enables restoring database dumps from production environments.

name: Hexagonal Architecture
description: The project applies Hexagonal Architecture (ports & adapters) to isolate business domain logic from technical concerns. The carpool-domain module contains exclusively domain entities (data class), use cases (fun interface) and ports (repository interfaces). Adapters (REST controllers, DAOs, SPI implementations) live in the app module. This separation ensures the domain is testable without any Spring dependency, and that technical implementations are interchangeable.

name: GitOps
description: The project adopts the GitOps model for all deployments: Kubernetes manifests (HelmRelease) are versioned in Git and reconciled by FluxCD. Every environment change goes through a pull request, ensuring traceability, code review and rollback capability. CI workflows (cd-integration.yml, deploy.yaml) only update image tags in Git; FluxCD handles cluster reconciliation.

name: Feature Toggles with Togglz
description: Feature toggles are implemented via Togglz, wrapped in eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-togglz-api. Features are defined in an enum annotated with @FeatureToggles, and constants are automatically generated by the KSP processor common-togglz-processor. The @OnActiveFeature annotation gates method execution on toggle activation. Toggle state can be managed via the Actuator in production, enabling progressive rollouts without redeployment.

name: Conventional Commits
description: The project enforces Conventional Commits on all pull requests via the conventionnal-commit.yml workflow. This commit message standard (feat:, fix:, chore:, etc.) is the foundation for automated semantic versioning by Release Please. It also improves git history readability and CHANGELOG.md generation. Validation is automatic on each PR, ensuring consistent history across the project.

name: OpenAPI-first API Design
description: The project follows an OpenAPI-first approach for REST API documentation. The app module integrates eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-open-api, which automatically configures SpringDoc/Swagger UI. The internal @EpRestDocumentedController annotation enriches the generated documentation. A dedicated Swagger UI is exposed per environment (at /swagger-ui/index.html), facilitating manual testing and API exploration by frontend teams and partners.

name: PR Preview Environments
description: Pull request preview environments can be triggered via the /preview command in a PR comment. The cd-previews.yml workflow automatically publishes images and deploys an ephemeral environment on the Kubernetes previews cluster. This practice shortens the feedback loop for feature reviews and enables product validation before merging. Each preview is accessible via a dedicated URL and is automatically destroyed when the PR is closed.

name: Database Audit with Hibernate Envers
description: Hibernate Envers is used for automatic JPA entity auditing via the eu.energypool.commons.tech:common-database-audit module. It creates audit tables (*_AUD) that track all changes (create, update, delete) with the author identity and timestamp. This feature is valuable for compliance and debugging, but its impact on performance and data volume should be assessed before enabling it on all entities.

name: Reusable CI/CD Workflows
description: The project leverages reusable GitHub Actions workflows (workflow_call) hosted in the shared repository energypool/gha_shared. Standardised workflows are called for Gradle builds, artefact publishing, CD deployments, Slack notifications and linting. This sharing model ensures CI/CD consistency across the organisation and simplifies maintenance: a fix in gha_shared automatically benefits all consuming projects.

name: OIDC / Zero Trust Security
description: The project applies Zero Trust principles for security: APIs are protected by OIDC via Keycloak (common-security-oidc), Kubernetes pods authenticate against AWS via IRSA (without static credentials), and application secrets are stored in AWS Secrets Manager with IAM-controlled access. In CI/CD, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens replace long-lived AWS access keys. This approach is the non-negotiable standard for all new services in the organisation.

name: Modular Monorepo
description: The project is organised as a multi-module monorepo covering the Kotlin/Spring Boot backend (6 Gradle modules) and the Angular frontend (1 module). This structure facilitates code sharing (the golden-path-spring-app-api module for shared DTOs, app-commons for constants), cross-module refactoring and dependency version consistency. The Gradle build cache optimises compilation times by only rebuilding modified modules.

name: AWS Secrets Manager
description: AWS Secrets Manager is used to store and distribute sensitive credentials (database passwords, JWT keys, OIDC secrets) outside of code and configuration files. The AWS JDBC Wrapper driver with the awsSecretsManager plugin automatically retrieves PostgreSQL connection credentials from Secrets Manager at startup. Secrets are referenced by SSM path in HelmRelease values (springConfigOverride.secrets), eliminating any plaintext secret from Kubernetes manifests.
